search_row.title: Declining force of selection with age
search_row.statement: The strength of selection on survival falls with age after reproduction begins, so senescence is an inevitable outcome of natural selection.
search_row.math: s(a) = \frac{\partial r}{\partial \ln p_a} = \frac{1}{T}\sum_{x=a+1}^{\infty} e^{-rx} l_x m_x, non-increasing in a

fields.dct:source: W. D. Hamilton (1966) The moulding of senescence by natural selection
fields.delphi:proposedTest: Compare age trajectories of mortality and fertility across many species with the trajectories that s(a) predicts from each species' own life table.
fields.delphi:context: Assumptions: an age-structured population with fixed age-specific fertility and no growth or repair after maturity. Formal status: the formula for s(a) is proved. The inevitability claim is refuted as stated: Jones et al. (2013) found species with flat or declining mortality with age, consistent with life histories where fertility rises with size.
